title: City to spend $500K on parking study despite recently paying for similar one
text:
SAN ANTONIO - The city is about to spend $500 thousand to study parking and mobility issues resulting from Project Marvel, the Downtown Sports and Entertainment
by Jaie Avila / News 4 San AntonioSAN ANTONIO - The city is about to spend $500 thousand to study parking and mobility issues resulting from Project Marvel, the Downtown Sports and Entertainment District that will include a new Spurs arena.
A study by Centro and the City of San Antonio which was just released in March found downtown as a whole has plenty of parking spaces. However, parking demand in the Project Marvel area could exceed the supply by as much as six thousand spaces.
At a council meeting earlier this month Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones expressed frustration that the council hadn't received an update on the new study which she felt had expanded in scope in the last few months.
“A study that will evaluate parking as one component of a broader downtown integrated mobility system at a cost of $500,000 to me that is a significant update," the mayor said. “The scope is essentially roughly the same," said the City’s Chief of Financial and Administrative Services Ben Gorzell.
City staff says the only thing that's changed about the study is that it now has an estimated price tag, and the name, which was changed from a parking study to a mobility study because some on the council thought too much emphasis was being placed on cars.
“Really, why we changed the name of it, was I got feedback from a couple of folks, from you all, that we give the implication that because we call it a parking feasibility study that we're interested in trying to solve in terms of how to build more parking," Gorzell said before council. Now the city seems to be leaning away from creating more parking.
A new parking garage next to the Alamodome prominently featured in early renderings of the district may not be built.
“We hope to solve that a different way and not have to build that garage. Maybe it's a garage built somewhere else, maybe it's not a garage at all," Gorzell said. The city tells the I-Team: "The study will look at the feasibility of new and existing city-owned parking facilities, the use of existing private parking, expected increases in via ridership, and the role of transportation network companies such as rideshare services.
" The city and Centro just paid for a parking study this year by Walker Consultants that looked at things like "future parking demand" and "transit service and event mobility". That study states: ". . . there is likely to be a localized parking deficit in the area surrounding the Sports and Entertainment District, particularly when simultaneous events occur.
"We asked why the city can't use it instead of paying for another study, but we did not receive a response on that. “The City is moving forward with a downtown mobility and access study, which was previously referred to as a parking feasibility study. The title has changed because staff wants to evaluate parking as one part of a broader downtown mobility system — not as a stand-alone decision about whether to build a new garage near the Alamodome.
The study will look at the feasibility of new and existing City-owned parking facilities, the use of existing private parking, expected increases in VIA ridership, and the role of transportation network companies such as rideshare services. The goal is to identify the best mix of parking, transit, pedestrian access, rideshare, and traffic-management strategies to support the Sports & Entertainment District and broader downtown activity. The study is estimated to cost $500,000 and will be funded through the Parking Enterprise Fund.
The RFP was released April 15, with City Council consideration of a consultant contract expected in June. Staff anticipates eight to 12 weeks of consultant and staff work, with draft findings expected in September.
